A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hybrid event-based object detection work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary materials are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and a changed title.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gen1/Gen4 detection results, component and architecture ablations, quantization experiments, and Loihi 2 power and latency measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original detection and hardware results and adds recurrent-model experiments, DWConvLSTM ablations and computational analyses.

M1.justification: V2 adds a hybrid+RNN variant with two DWConvLSTM units in the ANN backbone, combining fast SNN processing with longer-term recurrent processing (Section 3.2, Figure 1). This introduces substantial temporal-memory capability. The original SAT/ERS bridge and non-recurrent hybrid remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate automotive event-based object detection on Gen1 and Gen4 with the same class coverage. The recurrent configurations and additional comparisons use these existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds reported comparisons with RVT-B without LSTM and S4D/S5 models, plus a trained all-ANN control (Tables 1, 3 and 6). RED, ASTMNet and recurrent RVT comparators were already present. The numerical Gen4 no-ASAB baseline comparison disappears, while its Gen1 counterpart moves into Table 4. Table 2 also lists SpikeFPN alongside FP-DAGNet, although their closely overlapping references and identical reported scores leave their distinctness unclear.

E3.justification: The new RNN experiments introduce sequence length 21, 400,000 training steps and batch size 2, substantially extending the temporal training design (Section 4.1). V2 also introduces an all-ANN control and MAC/AC-based computational evaluation. Existing base-model epoch counts and 5-ms/50-ms timing remain. Cropping is newly listed among augmentations, but whether this changes the earlier procedure is unclear.

E4.justification: V2 adds DWConvLSTM placement ablations testing four-, three- and two-layer recurrent configurations (Table 8), and computational analyses testing the costs of ANN processing, the bridge and additional SNN layers (Section 5.2). Existing attention-component, SNN/ANN-depth and quantization studies remain; the no-ASAB Gen1 row is relocated evidence rather than a new ablation.

E5.justification: Both supplements report the same hardware means and standard deviations over 12 inputs and 100k steps. V2's abbreviated main-text hardware table does not remove the full uncertainty reporting retained in Table 10. Neither version reports detection-training seeds, repeated-run uncertainty or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports hybrid+RNN mAP of 0.43 on Gen1 and 0.34 on Gen4 under the new configuration; original hybrid values remain 0.35 and 0.27. Table 6 adds 1.63e9 MACs and 0.97e9 ACs for the hybrid versus 15.34e9 MACs for the ANN control. Gen4 comparator scores are added, while several Gen4 baseline and SNN mAP(.5) entries disappear. Section 5.1 changes the int8 accuracy entry to 0.343, but both supplementary quantization tables retain 0.349, leaving an inconsistent reported revision.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8) retain the event representation, PLIF dynamics, attention operations and hardware-scaling mathematics. Tensor renaming, equivalent delta notation and correction of the Psi typesetting do not introduce new mathematical reasoning. No theorem, proof or formal assumption is added.

C1.justification: V2's abstract, introduction and conclusion add multi-timescale recurrent processing as a central contribution. The abstract and contribution list extend the performance-comparability claim from ANN methods to ANN and RNN methods. The original attention bridge and neuromorphic implementation claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's short-window qualification about comparisons with RVT with arguments about recurrent inference, recomputation and arithmetic intensity. It also interprets recurrent-layer placement and computational tradeoffs. A new problem appears in the Gen4 discussion: it compares the hybrid's 0.27 with AEGNN's 0.16, although Table 1 assigns the latter to Gen1 and provides no Gen4 AEGNN result.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the recurrent training recipe, approximately six-day training time and expanded architecture table. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit Gen1/Gen4 bounding-box filtering thresholds and Gen4 resizing to 640×360. Table 9 also introduces inconsistent recurrent-layer output dimensions. These materially alter reproducibility information; omitted preprocessing details do not establish that the underlying procedures changed.

R1.justification: Related Work substantially expands discussion of directly relevant hybrid research, including Kugele et al., Aydin et al., DashNet, hybrid top-down attention and general hybrid frameworks. It also adds state-space models and LEOD. This broadens the immediate research positioning beyond v1's largely generic hybrid discussion, while several application-background and slow-feature references disappear.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and comparison narrative. Related Work becomes a separate section, hardware/computational analysis becomes a standalone section, and channel-grouping explanations and the SNN-depth ablation move into the supplement. The supplementary duplicate abstract is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn with recurrent connections; SAT and ERS diagrams are combined; qualitative comparisons are split between main text and supplement, with one Gen4 example omitted. Benchmark tables are reorganized and expanded, and new computational and recurrent-ablation tables are added. The main-text hardware table summarizes measurements already present in v1's supplement.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's explicit short-temporal-window limitation with an implemented recurrent variant and supporting ablations. The all-ANN control also provides more direct evidence for the computational-efficiency argument. These benefits are partly offset by removed preprocessing specifications, inconsistent int8 accuracy reporting, and errors in the new architecture table and Gen4 interpretation. The additions strengthen the paper, but the reproducibility and consistency problems limit the overall gain.
